(p-١) Surah At-Tur (The Mount)

Its central purpose is to establish the occurrence of the punishment, which is the content of the threat sworn to occur in Surah adh-Dhariyat, and which is the content of the warning whose truthfulness is indicated in Qaf. For its occurrence is more certain and more possible than the mountains which the Truthful One (al-Sadiq) reported would move, and He made the crumbling of some of them a sign of that; and [it is more certain than] the Book in its most established state, since it can be washed away and burned; and than the house, whose inhabitant or another can ruin it; and the roof, whose raiser can lower it; and the sea, which whoever kindles it can cause to flood. It has become clear that its name is the most indicative of this, through considering the oath and its answer, and even through the individual words in its address: (In the name of Allah) the Mighty King, possessor of dominion and sovereignty; (the Most Merciful, al-Rahman) whose mercy encompasses with compassion whoever realizes Him; (the Most Compassionate, al-Rahim) who singles out with His mercy and His guidance the people of devout obedience (al-qunut).

* *

When adh-Dhariyat was concluded with the establishing of the threat, this surah opened with affirming the punishment, which is the spirit of the threat. So He, exalted is He, said: ﴿By the Mount﴾. This is because, when they used to say about what the Messenger ﷺ brought: "It is only magic and illusion, with no reality [behind it]" (p-٢), He swore by the mountain, which is with them and with others of the people of intellect, the most established, most firm and hardest of the earth, and He expressed it by "al-Tur," which is shared between any mountain in general and the one attributed to Sinai, where the prophethood of Musa (peace be upon him) took place and where much of His Book was sent down, and other things, [as] signs known to the Children of Israel, who would seek counsel from them, ask them about the Prophet ﷺ, and be content with their statements about him. Among its signs: mercy was present in it through the intimate conversation of Musa (peace be upon him), and what was written for him in it on tablets of jewel, and what was sent down to him of the Torah, which He made a guidance, mercy, admonition, reminder, and a detailed explanation of everything. And there was also punishment in it, through the thunderbolt that struck them and caused them to die, then Allah revived them, and through the cloud they witnessed that enveloped it, so that it was like the smoke of a furnace; there were lightning flashes in it like the greatest fire seen; and trumpets blaring with a terrifying sound; and the crumbling of the mountain at the time of the theophany, and the swooning of Musa (peace be upon him), besides other signs that dispel darkness. Also, al-Tur is every mountain that produces vegetation, and the growth of a mountain is marvelous, for its growth does not occur except by a cause, and the cause of plants is water, and water is spread throughout the earth due to its being layered upon it, and it is equivalent to what has been uncovered of the water of the seas; and the higher the land rises, the further it is from water, and mountains are the furthest from it. So the cause of their growth is very hidden, known only to Allah and to whomever He grants understanding of it.

(p-3) Since the earth is the tablet of the heaven, from which the threat comes, and the mountains are the hardest of it, He mentioned the greatest of them in sign, namely Mount Sinai (Tur Sina). And since the Book is the tablet of the writer, and the divine Books are the most firmly established of books, and Tur Sina is the place in which a divine Book descended, He said: ﴿And a Book﴾, and affirmed its matter by His saying: ﴿inscribed﴾, that is, written in a uniform manner, in lines arranged of letters in an ordered sequence, comprising words in agreement, like the Book of Moses, upon him be peace, which He sent down to him and spoke with him much of it at the Tur. Its indefiniteness is for magnification, because if what is meant by it is the divine Books, then it is the most established of things; and if what is meant is the Qur'an specifically, then it is the most established of them, for none can alter its words; and if what is meant is the scroll of the Quraysh, then they had considered it the most established of covenants. He mentioned the strongest thing in which something is written, and the hardest and most perfectly made of it, and so He said:

in a parchment (riqq) unrolled (manshur)—meaning: in a skin prepared with a layer of scraping (qishr) for writing, made ready for reading and for taking admonition from what is in it. It is possible that by it He meant all the revealed Books, generally after specifically. Al-Razi said: al-Sadiq said: Indeed God manifested Himself to His servant through His Book as He manifested Himself through the Mount (al-Tur) when the latter was a locus of manifestation in creation, and the Book when it was a locus of manifestation in command; He combined the two in one verse (qarn). End of quotation.

It is also possible that by it He, glory be to Him, meant the document of injustice which they wrote, in which they agreed that they would not keep company with the Banu Hashim (p-4), nor speak to them, nor trade with them, nor consult them, nor intermarry with them, nor support them, nor deal with them, until they handed over to them the Messenger of God (ﷺ). They hung it inside the Ka'bah. So the Banu Hashim withdrew to the valley (shi'b) of Abu Talib, behind Abu Qubays, and the Banu al-Muttalib, the kin (rahṭ) of our Imam al-Shafi'i (may God be pleased with him), followed them, and they sided with them from among the Banu Abd Manaf. That was the cause of their honour throughout the ages. Then God sent the termite (al-arada) upon the document—after two years had passed over that, when hardship afflicted them, time pressed them, and calamities shook them with a mighty shaking, while they remained steadfast—so that God might thereby show the honour of whomever He wills of His servants. It left intact whatever in it was of the names of God, Exalted, and erased what was of their injustice and severance of ties. That became the reason for a group among them rising to annul it, and God annulled it through them, and at that time they were all disbelievers, so that God might manifest His power, glory be to Him, over each of annulment and confirmation, with whatever and whomever He wills.

﴿And the House that is frequented﴾, which is a means of sustenance (qiyam) for the people, just as the Qubbat al-Zaman (the tabernacle of the age) was a means of sustenance for the Children of Israel. This is if He, exalted is He, meant by it the Ka'bah, in which they hung the Sahifah (the scroll), after they had rebuilt it and disagreed over who should place the Black Stone (al-Hajar al-Aswad) in its place. The disagreement increased among them until they readied themselves for fighting and swore alliances over it. Among them were the La'qat al-Dam (those who licked the blood), and among them were the Mutayyibun (those who dipped their hands in perfume), as is well known in the biographies. Then they were granted success in agreeing that the first person to enter through a gate they designated should judge between them. The first to enter through it was the Prophet (ﷺ). They all said: "This is Muhammad, the trustworthy. We are content with his judgment." So he (ﷺ) ruled that the noble stone be placed in a garment, and that the chief of each tribe take hold of one of its corners and they all lift it together. When it reached its place, he (ﷺ) took it with his noble hand and set it in its place. Thus his honour was doubled, through his judgment and his reconciling them, and his being singled out for placing it, while the House was thronged with visitors, its service, and a great retinue.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 52, verse 5:

Since the house (al-bayt) must in its meaning have a roof (saqf), He said: ﴿And the raised roof﴾, meaning the roof of the Ka'bah, as an indication that it is firmly built, its door closed, and its roof perfectly constructed, with a perfection greater than the perfection of the roof of the dome of time (qubbat al-zaman) in which the Children of Israel witnessed of the divine greatness and majesty what, if you asked them about it, they would tell you. Yet despite this, He gave power over the scroll (al-sahifah), which was in its interior, and perhaps it was in its roof where no one could reach it, to destroy it, establishing the reality of what He willed of His affair, as a warning of what He had threatened. It is also possible that what is meant by it, together with that, is the heaven (al-sama') in which is what you are promised. It is known to everyone of sound intellect that the lowest of roofs does not rise without pillars except by causes that are not seen, so how much more the heaven, which has such breadth, greatness and thickness, and what it contains of stars, with such qualities that minds cannot encompass its description, and they do not see its causes, as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Without pillars that you can see﴾ [al-Ra'd: 2]. It is related from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him and his father, that he said: it is the Throne ('arsh), and it is the roof of Paradise.

And since water is stronger than all that has preceded, He concluded with it, saying: (p-6) ﴿And by the sea that is filled (with fire/water)﴾. That is, the sea in which there is more water than its capacity, and "masjur" means "restrained" (sajirahu), i.e., prevented, just as a dog is prevented from swimming off by its leash (sajur). Had He willed, He would have let it loose, so it would have gushed forth and flowed, destroying whatever passed over it of mountain, book, and house, as was witnessed when He (Glorified is He) restrained it for the Children of Israel so that it split apart and its ground dried out. Then, when He willed to release it upon the family of Pharaoh, He punished them with it and destroyed them, so that not one of them remained.

When he swore by that which indicates the prophethood (nubuwwah) of Musa, peace be upon him, and then swore by that which alludes to the prophethood of Muhammad (ﷺ), and then by that which is common to both of them, and the first oath, along with that, indicated the stability of the earth, the third indicated its suitability for habitation, and the second indicated the Guardian in that, and he swore by the fourth, which completes the benefits and warns against falling, just as he warned with the first against being swallowed up by the earth, and he swore by the fifth, which indicates what was intended by the first, namely stability, because if there were any tilting, the sea would rush toward that side, he answered the oath with His saying: ﴿Indeed, the punishment of﴾. Since He, glorified is He, is of great honour toward him (ﷺ), He attributed the punishment to the attribute of kindness and the special nurture granted to him. He attributed the attribute to his pronoun, as a notification that He would show him in his community what would gladden him, and that the similarity of "their sins being like the sins of their predecessors" (cf. ﴿For those who did wrong there is a share like the share of their companions﴾, 51:59) lies only in mere humiliation, not in His uprooting them as He uprooted those. So He said: ﴿your Lord﴾, meaning the One who took charge of your nurture, whatever punishment He intends for everyone who intends harm to him, especially the one who opposes His friends, glorified is He, ﴿is surely going to occur﴾, meaning it is firmly established and will descend upon whoever intends the descent of something heavy (p-7) from a high place. Just as, if He willed, He could overturn the earth which He made firm and make the roof which He raised fall, and release the sea which He kept filled, as is known from His releasing the sea as a split path for the family of Pharaoh until He drowned them in it.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 52, verse 8:

﴿There is none to avert it.﴾ Because He has no partner in His position, by which these oaths point to the perfection of His power, the majesty of His wisdom, and His precise recording of the deeds of the servants for recompense, whether we say that the Book is the one the guardian angels write, or that it is the one that preserves the religion. So when He brought the punishment upon them in the Scroll, broke their covenant, and dispersed their gathering, He brought your company out of that constriction. Likewise He will support you until you strike them, break their assembly, crush their power, slay their leaders, and make your religion prevail over theirs, and those among them who remain become part of your party and helpers of your religion. Al-Baghawi said: Jubayr ibn Mut'im (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "I came to Madinah to speak with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about the captives of Badr. I found him praying the Maghrib prayer with his Companions, and his voice was coming out of the mosque. I heard him recite ﴿By the Mount﴾ [al-Tur: 1] up to his saying ﴿Indeed, the punishment of your Lord is bound to occur﴾ [al-Tur: 7], ﴿there is none to avert it.﴾ My heart was nearly torn when I heard it, and I had not yet embraced Islam that day, so I embraced Islam out of fear of the descent of the punishment. I did not think I would rise from my place until the punishment befell me." (p-8) Imam Abu Ja'far ibn al-Zubayr said: When Allah Most High threatened the disbelievers of Quraysh and whoever was on their path among all who denied the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), that they would suffer what befell other deniers of the nations, which was alluded to earlier in the surah, He then indicated, glorified is He, the magnitude of the disgrace and painful punishment that would reach them, by His saying: ﴿So woe to those who disbelieve from their day which they are promised﴾ [al-Dhariyat: 60]. He swore, glorified is He, to the truth of this and its occurrence (and we seek refuge in Him, glorified is He, from His wrath and painful punishment), saying, Most High: ﴿By the Mount﴾ [al-Tur: 1] up to His saying ﴿Indeed, the punishment of your Lord is bound to occur﴾ [al-Tur: 7], ﴿there is none to avert it.﴾ Then He pointed to those who deserve and merit it, saying ﴿So woe, that Day, to the deniers﴾ [al-Tur: 11]. Then He mentioned what they would be rebuked and reproached for, of their saying about him, upon him be prayers and peace, that he was a sorcerer, saying Most High: ﴿Taste the punishment of the Fire which you used to deny﴾ [Saba': 42], ﴿Is this magic, or do you not see?﴾ [al-Tur: 15]. Then He followed with mention of the state of the believers who responded. Then, after informing about the state of both groups, He mentioned His blessing upon His Prophet, upon him be prayers and peace, and His protection and safeguarding him from what the fabricators say, saying Most High: ﴿So remind, for by the favor of your Lord you are not a soothsayer or a madman﴾ [al-Tur: 29]. Then the verses continued in rebuking them for their speech and the weakness of their shifting claims: at one time they say "soothsayer," at another "madman," and at another "a poet awaiting his death." He rebuked them for all of that, exposed their lies, humbled them, and confounded what was in their hands by His saying: ﴿Then let them produce a statement like it, if they are truthful﴾ [al-Tur: 34]. (p-9) This is what undoes what they had fabricated, first and last, and this is what they found no answer to; they were content with the sword and exile and did not venture to attempt its opposition. This is what is referred to in His saying, Most High, at the beginning of Surah al-Baqarah: ﴿And if you are in doubt about what We have sent down upon Our servant, then produce a surah like it﴾ [al-Baqarah: 23], and the verses that follow; yet they did not utter a word in reply to it. ﴿Say: If mankind and the jinn gathered to produce the like of this Qur'an, they would not produce its like﴾ [al-Isra': 88]. Blessed is He who made it a dazzling sign and an overpowering proof. End.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 52, verse 9:

When he had established the occurrence of the punishment, the soul of the one with certainty yearned to know its time. He said, resuming in order to explain that it occurs in that description: ﴿On the Day when the sky will sway violently﴾, meaning it moves, quivers, comes and goes, sways like the rocking of a ship, turns like the turning of a millstone, and its parts surge over one another and differ from one another, yet it does not leave its place. Al-Baghawi said: "The word mawr (مَوْر) gathers all these meanings. In the language, it means going, coming, wavering, turning, and agitation." Al-Razi said: "It has also been said: it comes and goes like smoke, and then dissipates."

﴿The sky﴾, which is the roof of your house, the earth, ﴿will be in violent turmoil﴾, meaning intense agitation.

﴿And the mountains will move﴾, meaning they will shift from their places the way clouds move, and he confirmed its meaning with His saying: ﴿a moving﴾, so they will become scattered dust (p-10) and the earth will become a level, smooth plain.

Now that He has affirmed the punishment and specified its Day, He specifies its people by saying, as a consequence of that: ﴿Woe﴾ is a word people say to one who has fallen into destruction, and its meaning is the descent of a disgraceful evil in which there is lamentation and grief. ﴿On that Day﴾, i.e., the Day on which what has been mentioned before occurs. ﴿To the deniers﴾, i.e., those deeply rooted in denial, namely those who died while ascribing lying to the truthful.

Since denial can sometimes occur in its proper place, he clarified that what is meant is the denial of that whose proper place is truth, so he said: ﴿Those who are﴾, that is, from among people, in their outward and inward states, ﴿in plunging﴾, that is, their deeds and their statements are the deeds of one who plunges into water, for he does not know where to place his foot. Since that might arise from bewilderment about them or from grief, he negated that by saying: ﴿playing﴾. Thus two matters that necessitate falsehood combined in them: plunging and playing. They are such that no statement or action of theirs can properly occur in its place, so nothing is founded upon clarity or proof.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 52, verse 13:

When he had depicted their denial in its most hideous form, he explained their woe by stating the time of it and what is done in it, so he said: ﴿On the Day they are thrust﴾, that is, they are pushed with a violent shove, with harshness and brutality, by everything that Allah has appointed for that purpose, going forth and being driven ﴿into the Fire of Hell﴾, which is the tier that receives them with scowling, aversion, rage and roaring. He emphasized the meaning and affirmed it with His saying: ﴿with a thrusting﴾. (p-11) Al-Baghawi said: This is because the guardians of Hell raise their hands to their necks and gather their forelocks to their feet, then they are thrust headlong upon their faces and shoved in their napes, being told, as a rebuke and reproach:

This is the commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 52, verse 14:

﴿This is the Fire﴾ i.e., the burning body that destroys whatever it reaches, the one that diverts from idle play, ﴿which you used to﴾ by your corrupt natural dispositions. And since your denial of it was at the furthest degree of denial, and was the cause of every denial, it was as if denial were restricted to it; so he said, placing the adverbial phrase first to indicate this,

﴿deny it.﴾ That is, in the world, in renewal and continuation.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 52, verse 15:

When they were saying out of obstinacy that the Qur'an, with the threat it contains, is sorcery, he followed that threat with his words, rebuking, reproaching and mocking them: ﴿Is this sorcery? Or do you not see?﴾ That is, this punishment you are in, together with this burning which you are being roasted in. ﴿Or is it you who do not see﴾ in a dream or the like ﴿[are you] not perceiving?﴾ with the hearts, as you used to say in the world ﴿Our hearts are in coverings﴾ [Fussilat: 5], nor with the eyes, as you used to say to the warners ﴿And between us and you there is a barrier, so act, for we too are acting﴾ [Fussilat: 5]. That is: you are blind to the thing reported, even while it burns you, just as you were blind to the report. That is, can you say that you do not perceive the thing reported, as you used to say about the report, falsely and wickedly? Then, after this rebuke, which makes certain that their answer will be that they say: "No, by the might of our Lord, this is not sorcery nor imagination, but it is reality, (p-12) and we are in complete sight, by way of humiliation, abasement and disgrace":

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 52, verse 16:

﴿Roast in it﴾ i.e., experience its heat, endure it and keep at it, just as you used to persist in harming My servants with what burns their hearts. ﴿So be patient [or impatient]﴾ i.e., as a consequence of your denial in the world and your exposure to it now, it will be said to you: be patient with this, for which you have no capacity. ﴿Or do not be patient﴾ for there is no escape for you from it. ﴿It is all the same for you﴾ i.e., patience or impatience.

Since it is well known that patience has a distinction over impatience (jaza'), he made clear that this is the case where the affliction is only in the form of a recompense that must necessarily occur, so he said, giving the reason: ﴿You are only being recompensed﴾ i.e., your recompense occurs now and will continue forever, ﴿for what you used to do﴾ i.e., constantly, as a habit that has become your nature, ﴿[in dealing] with the friends [of God]﴾ without caring about them. So this was the fruit of what you did to them.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 52, verse 17:

When he (Allah) had mentioned what awaits those who deny, the punishment referred to by the oath-formulas, He followed it with what is for their opposites, the reward likewise alluded to by those same formulas, so that the report might be complete in both encouragement and warning. He said, answering one who would seem to have asked: "What, then, is for those who opposed them concerning You?" confirming what is due to the disbelievers by way of denial: ﴿Indeed, the God-fearing﴾, that is, those for whom taqwa (God-consciousness) has become a firm, settled quality, ﴿will be in gardens﴾, that is, orchards, lasting in this world in judgment and in the Hereafter.

And since orchards may at times be a place where its occupant or its owner suffers hardship, he negated this by His saying: (p-13) ﴿and bliss﴾, that is, bliss in the immediate (world), by means of the intimacy they are in, and in the deferred (Hereafter) in actuality. He increased the affirmation of enjoyment with His saying:

Fākihīn (ﷻ) means: joyful, delighting in ("mu'jabīn mutaladhdhidhīn") **﴿with what their Lord has given them﴾**, the One who took charge of their nurture, by their works of obedience, until He brought them to this bliss. Because of His greatness, He is the source of this greatness, and His true attributes cannot be fully described. And since one who enjoys luxury may have his blessing come after punishment, He clarified that they are not like that, saying: **﴿And their Lord has protected them﴾**, that is, before that, **﴿from the punishment of the Blazing Fire﴾**, that is, the Fire of intense blaze, by restraining them from sins and filth. The One who graciously nurtured them.

Since those who enjoyed the blessing and kept away from the punishment were in great ease, he said, rendering this as a translation on the assumption of a saying: ﴿Eat﴾, that is, eat with relish, ﴿and drink﴾, drink ﴿with relish﴾, that is, without any deficiency in it. It is an adjective in the place of the verbal noun, meaning "you have enjoyed," in the sense that everything you partake of is safe in its outcome from indigestion, sickness, and the like. ﴿For what you used to﴾, that is, as a firm state, ﴿do﴾, that is, renewing it continuously and steadily, until it became as if it were a natural disposition for you.

Since bliss is not complete unless the person is served, he draws attention to this with His words ﴿reclining﴾, meaning leaning in a state of ease, because they are served and have no need to move. ﴿On couches arranged in rows﴾, meaning set up one beside another, level, arranged in the finest and most inventive order. Al-Asbahani said: the *sifah* (the root sense of the word) is extending a thing in continuity.

Since joy is not complete without enjoying women, He said: ﴿And We gave them wives﴾, meaning a marriage fitting to Our greatness. (p-14) Since that abode is free of the means of contract, so that they were free of the need for a contract, He said, indicating with the *bā'* (بِ) that the verb is diverted from its apparent sense, for when it means marriage it takes its object directly, and by *tadmīn* (the implicit inclusion of one verb's meaning in another), the verb ﴿qaranāhum﴾ (قَرَنّاهُمْ) is taken to mean "We made them mates, joined in pairs" ﴿with ḥūr﴾, meaning women who possess, in an extreme that cannot be described, intense whiteness of the eye, intense blackness of it, roundness of the pupil, and fineness of the eyelids ﴿'īn﴾, meaning large-eyed, in radiance and beauty.
