**Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 52, verse 21:**

When he (Allah) had described the condition of the God-fearing (al-muttaqun) among the enemies of the deniers, and began with them because of their nobility, He followed them with those who are lower than them in rank, so that the blessing would be complete. So He said: ﴿And those who believed﴾, meaning: they affirmed faith, did not alter it, and did not go to excess in righteous deeds.

Since among these there are some whose descendants do not follow them because of their faith, as they apostatize from it, He added to their deed, as a distinction for them and a safeguard against those who did not firmly hold to his statement: ﴿and their descendants followed them﴾, that is, by what We possess of bounty arising from what We possess of greatness, ﴿their descendants﴾, the young and the old, however many they may be. The settling of their eyes comes through the elders by their own faith, and the young by the faith of their fathers. ﴿with faith﴾, that is, by means of a faith existing in them, even if it is at the lowest degrees of faith; but they remained steadfast upon it until they died, and that is the condition for their descendants following them. It is also permissible to mean, and this is closer: by the faith of the descendants in reality if they are adults, and by judgment if they are young. Then He informed about the relative (al-mawsul) with His statement: ﴿We will join them﴾, that is, by Our bounty, for the sake of their fathers' deeds, ﴿their descendants﴾, even if the descendants have no deeds of their own, because it has been said regarding this meaning: "For the sake of one eye, a thousand eyes are honored." (p-15) And there joins the descendants of lineage the descendants by cause, which is love. If there is with it someone who takes knowledge or deed, that is more fitting, so the descendants of benefit are like the descendants of birth. This is based on the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "A person is with whom he loves," in answer to one who asked about someone who loves a people but has not joined them.

Since it might be feared that the fathers would be diminished in some of their ranks because their descendants are joined to them, He said: ﴿And We did not deprive them﴾, that is, We did not diminish the fathers and did not withhold from them ﴿of their deeds﴾, and He emphasized the negation with His statement: ﴿of anything﴾, because of this joining. The rank above theirs, of those who believe, the believers, the God-fearing and others, is more deserving than them. He separated them from those because these may not be certain, before entering Paradise, of the punishment. He said, gathering both groups, or it is said (and this is perhaps closer) that when He mentioned the lower following the higher in good as a favor, the soul feared that it might be following in evil, so the Exalted answered by saying that He does not do so, with His statement: ﴿Every person﴾, that is, of those who believed, the God-fearing and others, ﴿for what he earned﴾, that is, of children and others, ﴿is held in pledge﴾, that is, is a stake, is at risk, is one who is sought, takes something in place of his earnings, is repaid according to what he deserves, and is held back by it if he is disobedient. So whoever is righteous, he is taking by means of his child's righteousness, because it is his earnings, and he is not seized by it in humiliation, and it is good in itself because of the judgment of his faith, whether in reality or by judgment, and every good is elevated, so for this reason he is joined to his father. As for evil, it is confined to its owner; he is seized by it and held in pledge for his sin, and not seized for the sin of another. The summary is that the excellences, which are like life, overflow from their owner to others and give them life, while the evils, which are like death, do not pass beyond their owner. Al-Razi said in al-Lawami': Know that the essences, their continuance and permanence are by the continuance of their forms; wherever the form that sustains them is more lasting, the essences are more upright by it. The human souls are essences, and their forms are their knowledge and their morals. Wherever the knowledge is the truth of certainty and then the very certainty, and the morals are established upon the path of the clear Shari'ah, the souls are enduring by its permanence, not subject to annihilation, and neither coming into being nor corrupting, since the very certainty and true knowledge are not of the world of becoming and corruption. Even if the soul does not reach the perfection of certainty, it clings to the proof of its companion, just as it is strung in its thread, until a person is strung in the thread of his love. "If one of you loved a stone, he would be gathered with it." For religion is love for the sake of Allah and hatred for the sake of Allah. For this reason the Shari'ah is content from the obligated with Islam, submission, entrusting, and seeking judgment, without standing upon intricate matters with clear and sound proofs. As for a child who has not reached the limit of obligation and dies, they are joined to their fathers, and judgment is passed upon them by the judgment of their beliefs and opinions, so that their fathers' judgment applies to them and the judgment of the Resurrection is enforced upon them. As for when the form existing in the essences is subject to change, being ignorance and falsehood whose first part diminishes its last and whose last diminishes its first, the essence of the soul is not annihilated nor perishes, but remains in a state in which it neither dies nor lives, for if it perished it would find rest, and if it remained it would find pleasure. So it is in a state of change between death and life, and this change occurs only in bodies and physical frames: ﴿Every time their skins are roasted through, We will replace them with other skins﴾ [an-Nisa': 56]. End of quotation.

He is, as you see, most precious. It is supported by: "A man is raised upon the religion of his close friend, so let each of you look at whom he takes as a friend." It is also permissible that the sentence is a reason for what precedes of negation, meaning: We did not diminish them, because it has already preceded in Our judgment that "every person" We decreed to be held in pledge by what may diminish him ﴿for what he earned﴾, that is, what another earned does not harm him ﴿is held in pledge﴾, that is, he is hindered from bliss until he brings what releases him of righteous deed.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 52, verse 22:

When He gathered them together in the joining of their offspring to them, because that is among the greatest of blessings, and assured them against what might be feared of their deficiency by means of His deficiency toward others, and gave the reason for that so that it would be more firmly fixed in the soul, He followed it with what is similar to it, saying: ﴿And We will provide them﴾, that is, those who believed and the God-fearing and those of their offspring who were joined to them, ﴿with fruit﴾ by what We possess of greatness, as an increase beyond what has preceded. ﴿With fruit﴾: since fruit is manifest in what they know in this world, although the life of the Garden includes all things for enjoyment (tafakkuh), with nothing in it aimed at preserving the body, He said: ﴿and meat from whatever they desire﴾, with nothing in it of what would not please them to the utmost degree of pleasure.

Since this great and enduring bounty calls to companionship, with fragrant mates, He explained that this is their constant and evident condition, among the fine and pure qualities, so He said: ﴿They pass around among themselves﴾, i.e., they drink, pulling at one another in playful pulling, out of excessive love and joy and the adornment of companionship, ﴿a cup﴾, i.e., wine, whose rim is so delicate that it is almost invisible in its cup. And since the wine of this world has harmful consequences, He negated them, so He said: ﴿No idle talk﴾, i.e., no nonsense of what harms and does not benefit, ﴿in it﴾ (p-18), i.e., in their passing it around, nor because of it, for it does not take away their reason, and they speak only what is good and beautiful, ﴿nor any sinfulness﴾, i.e., there is nothing in it of what would attach to its drinkers as sin, nor is it fitting to attribute such a thing to it.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 52, verse 24:

Since the serving of drink (al-mu'aṭāh) cannot be complete in its spread nor magnificent except with attendants and cupbearers, He said: ﴿And there will go around them⁠ — that is, with cups and other kinds of luxurious vessels — ﴾ ﴿boys⁠﴾ belonging to them. And since the dearest thing to a person is what is specific to him, He said: ﴿to them⁠﴾, and He did not attribute them (to the people of Paradise by a possessive pronoun in the sense of "their boys" as servants of this world) lest it be supposed that they are the very ones who used to serve them in this world, so that everyone who served someone in this world, by word or deed, would fear that he would be his servant in Paradise and would grieve at remaining a follower forever. The indefinite form (tankīr) also conveys that everyone who enters Paradise finds servants for himself whom he did not know before that. ﴿As if they were⁠﴾ in their whiteness and the intensity of their purity ﴿pearls, well-guarded⁠﴾ — that is, protected within the shell, not altered by any accidents. This is the state of the servant; so what do you suppose of the one served?

Since the most delightful thing to the beloved, and the greatest of his desires, is the remembrance of his Beloved and praise of Him for the blessings He has bestowed, He—exalted is He—said, explaining this and linking it to what is implied by the context, meaning: "So turn to partaking of the blessings mentioned":

﴿And they will approach one another, questioning each other﴾, because of the joy that delighted them and the pleasure and happiness that pleased them. That is, some of them ask others about the cause that brought them to this bliss, which no created being can describe as it truly deserves to be described.

(p-19) Then he resumed explaining this with his saying: ﴿They said﴾, meaning each of them said, emphatically, savouring what had brought them to their present state, because it is hardly believable. They ascribed the blessing, through the verb "to be," to God, who created them with a disposition toward goodness. They omitted the preposition, indicating the continuity of their fear, as a reminder that the fear which restrains one from sins must be continuous, unlike the hope which motivates acts of obedience, for that only requires what is within one's ability. Its indication will come by affirming the preposition: ﴿Indeed we were before﴾, meaning in the abode of action, ﴿among our family﴾, with what they had of number, equipment, blessing and abundance, and for us, from them, the sources of pleasure and the motives to play, ﴿fearful﴾, meaning deeply fearful of God, nothing diverting us from that, together with our adherence to what we were able to do of His obedience, knowing that we cannot give Him His due measure in His greatness, majesty, grandeur and perfection, and that if He took us to account for our smallest sins, He would destroy us. Al-Razi said: al-Ishfaq (solicitude, anxious care) is the continuance of caution combined with compassion, that one is compassionate toward the self before it rushes into obstinacy. It has divisions: solicitude regarding the deed, that it come to ruin; solicitude regarding creation, for knowing their measures; solicitude regarding time, that it be mixed with dispersal; and regarding the heart, that some incidental thing mix with it; and regarding the self, that some cause enter into it. End of quotation.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 52, verse 27:

When He, glory be to Him, related of them that they attributed to themselves a deed, as a lesson for whoever He wills happiness, so that it would appear that they saw it as the cause of what they had attained, they said, negating this supposition and making clear that what they are in is, from the beginning, a bounty from Allah, exalted is He, because their apprehension of Him, glory be to Him, is so that a person does not rely on anything of his deed, and thus he is always magnifying his Lord and fearing Him: ﴿So Allah has bestowed favor upon us﴾, He who possesses all perfection, because of our apprehension of Him, ﴿upon us﴾ with what befits His perfection, so He granted us security, ﴿and protected us﴾, that is, He kept us away, by that with which He covered us, ﴿from the punishment of the scorching wind﴾, that is, the heat that penetrates the pores as poison penetrates.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 52, verse 28:

When they mentioned their apprehensiveness, they explained it, emphasizing again with the like of that by their saying: ﴿Indeed we were﴾, that is, by what we were disposed to and made ready for. Since supplication (du'a') carries the meaning of performing worship, and it occurs at some times, he affirmed the preposition (al-jarr) as an indication of that, while omitting it before this in "in supplication" (fi al-du'a') with strength (bil-quwwa), as an indication that adorning oneself with virtues (al-tahalli bil-fada'il) is accepted from one with ease, whereas emptying oneself of vices (al-takhalli 'an al-radha'il) necessarily requires freedom from every little and much. So it is said: ﴿from before﴾, that is, in the worldly life, ﴿we used to call upon Him﴾, that is, we used to ask Him and worship Him in actuality. As for our fear in potentiality, it was in every movement and stillness. Then they gave the reason for their calling upon Him, emphasizing that His bestowing favor upon them despite their shortcomings is something that almost no one else would do, so it is among the things at which one marvels to the utmost degree. So they said: ﴿Indeed He, He﴾, that is, alone, ﴿is the Benevolent (al-Barr)﴾, the one of wide generosity whose giving is wisdom and whose withholding is mercy, because giving does not diminish Him and withholding does not increase Him. He shows kindness to His believing servant by what agrees with the servant's soul; so perhaps He shows kindness to him with blessing, and perhaps He shows kindness to him with hardship. He chooses for him from among the states what is better for him, so that He may enlarge for him in the hereafter. Therefore, it is incumbent upon the believer not to accuse his Lord regarding any of His decrees. ﴿The Merciful (al-Rahim)﴾, the one who honors whomever He wills among His servants by enabling them to act in what He is pleased with of obedience to Him, then by bounty upon them even if they fall short in His service. (p-21)

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 52, verse 29:

Since this, together with its arousing of desire for Paradise and for the deeds that lead to it, is an exhortation that softens hearts and dispels distress, He made the following statement its consequence: ﴿So remind⁠﴾, that is, renew the reminding with the like of this for everyone who hopes for its good, and persist in that. He called it "reminding" because it is among the things a person knows when he looks carefully into himself or into the horizons. He gave the reason for the reminding in His saying: ﴿So you are not⁠﴾, that is, while you are the most noble of people in lineage, the most complete of them in soul, and the purest of them in character, which they acknowledged in you before prophethood, ﴿by the grace of your Lord⁠﴾, that is, by means of what your Lord, who has bestowed kindness upon you, bestowed upon you of this supreme law (nāmūs) after qualifying you for it by what He prepared you with of soundness of intellect, loftiness of aspiration, nobility of conduct, generosity of hand, purity of morals, and nobility of descent. He emphasized the negation with His saying: ﴿a soothsayer⁠﴾, that is, one who speaks words, despite their being contrived rhymed prose (saj'), most of which are empty, and who judges unseen matters by things that happen, some of which contradict one another. Since the soothsayer and the madman have a connection with the jinn, He followed that with His saying: ﴿nor a madman⁠﴾, that is, one who speaks words without any order, together with reporting some unseen matters. So let their saying this not turn you away from reminding, for it is a false saying to which no blemish whatsoever will attach you. Before long it will be a shame upon them that nothing will wash away from them except following you. Whoever of them follows you washes away his disgrace, and whoever persists in his obstinacy, his ruin and loss will persist.

(p-22) Since the attribution to him ﷺ, in what he brought them of this Qur'an which enjoins wisdom, was that he brought it from the jinn, whose nature is corruption, something that no one should even imagine, let alone say to him ﷺ, and it is hardly credible that anyone would accuse him of it, there was implicit in it a question of rebuke and reproach. He drew attention to this by the conjunction (ʿaṭf) upon what is in the sense of: "Do they say this saying, far-fetched from the sayings of people of intellect?" ﴿Or do they say﴾ that which is more wondrous, merely in his uttering it, let alone repeating it. So "am" (ʾam) here is equivalent (muʿādilah) to the interrogative before it, not disjunctive (maqṭūʿah), and so is everything that follows it. This is the meaning of what al-Baghawi transmitted from al-Khalil, that he said: "Everything in Surat al-Tur that contains the mention of 'am' is interrogative and not a conjunction."

﴿A poet﴾ who says speech that is metrical by deliberate intent, to whom artificiality is necessary for that, so that the imposition of meter overcomes its speaker until he makes the wording the principal and makes the meaning follow it. Thus much of his speech comes out deficient in meanings, loosely woven, overpowered in his own affair, admitting his shortcoming when he examines it, pleading in excuse what he thinks has adorned it of its meters. Glorified is He, who put this, and likewise what follows it of the divisions (of questions), in the form of interrogation, although their attribution to them is established, as an alert that the like of this is not said by an intelligent person, and if someone has said it, the transmitter from him would hardly believe it.

(p-23) ﴿We await for him﴾, i.e., we wait, ﴿the vicissitudes of fate﴾, i.e., the calamities of time, from death and other things that cut off, from "al-mann," which is cutting.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 52, verse 31:

Since it was as if it were said to them, "They indeed say that," he said, informing them of his response: ﴿Say: Wait; indeed I am with you among those who wait.﴾ He did not turn aside to argue with them in their saying this, as a reminder that it is of such worthlessness that no refutation by debate is needed for it. Then he made the consequence of his command to them to wait his saying: ﴿Indeed I am with you﴾, and he emphasized it as a reminder that he hopes for their joy at his calamity just as they hope for joy at his calamity, even though their large numbers and strength were preventing them from such waiting in their own eyes, ﴿among those who wait﴾, that is, the most diligent of those who wait, even if you suppose otherwise. By "with" he indicated that he is equal to them in this, even though they thought, because of their large numbers and strength and his singularity and weakness, that the matter was otherwise.

Al-Qushayri said: It has been related in the tafsir that all of them, that is, those who waited for him, died. He said: No one should hope for the decline of his market through the death of someone so that the turn comes to him; few are those of whom this is the description who are not overtaken by death, and he does not attain what he wished for of that hope.

Al-Biqa'i, Nazm al-Durar, on Surah 52, verse 32:

Since their statement is of a kind that is not said at all, and even if it were said, it is so far-fetched that it seems to have been uttered as a slip of the tongue or something similar, he drew attention to it by an antithetical question whose implied meaning is: "Did they say that out of heedlessness?" ﴿Or do their intellects command them to this?﴾ That is, does their own mind enjoin upon them such a thing, an adornment that leads their end to be a driving compulsion like a command? ﴿Their intellects﴾ means their minds, which they claim were distinguished by their excellence over other people, to the extent that it was said of them: "possessors of intellects and restraint" (p-24), ﴿by this﴾, that is, while they believe in its soundness and that it is the just and equitable [judgment], because they are bound by intellect and restraint despite the corruption in it through contradiction, after each statement individually collapses, as was explained earlier. This is a severe rebuke, by way of indication that they have no intellects at all in view of this statement. For a soothsayer, according to them, must be at the utmost of knowledge, to the point that they make him a judge and sometimes worship him. A madman is not fit for any righteous matter, for he does not reason. And a poet is far from such matters given the metrical structure and abundance of speech, which is like the rhymed prose of the soothsayer and others, and the speech of a madman. ﴿Or are they a people﴾ in their outward and inward states, ﴿who are transgressors?﴾ That is, possessed of strength to carry out what they attempt, and therefore ﴿transgressing﴾, that is, exceeding the limits. This is a habit of theirs, as the description conveys. Therefore they do not care about manifest obstinacy in opposing what intellect and restraint command, and none says this except the tyrannical and foolish while the truth is evident to them. They speak contradictory words, caring for no one and not ashamed of being attributed to hostility and extreme disobedience. The verse is of the kind called *ihtibak*: it mentions "intellects" first as an indication of their opposite second, and "transgression" second as an indication of its opposite "the just and equitable" first. Its secret is that what is mentioned is more effective in repelling evil and more powerful in disparaging it and warning against it.

Tafsir (exegesis) of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on Surah 52, verse 33:

﴿Or do they say, "He has fabricated it"?﴾ What is more disgraceful than contradiction: ﴿Taqawwalahu﴾, that is, he contrived his speech from his own self, (p-25) as a lie. It is not poetry, nor soothsaying, nor madness. And they, despite their multitude, some of them being learned in knowledge and others being eloquent in poetry, oratory, rhymed prose (tarassul) and sajʿ, are unable to produce its like, indeed unable to produce anything resembling a part of it. Since speech is in reality in the self, and they knew the falsehood of everything they say of that kind, the implication is: they did not say any of that in reality and conviction. ﴿Rather, they do not believe﴾, that is, they do not acknowledge the truth while knowing the falsehood of their statement and its contradiction, out of obstinacy on their part, not as disbelief in the inner heart.

When this statement was clearer in its falsehood than anything else they had said, because their denial of him, even on their own assumption that he had invented it, does not depend on anything outside his power, He challenged them to a counter-attempt (*mu'aradah*, producing a rival), since if they produced its like the dispute would be settled. For this reason He linked to what preceded it a statement denying their claim, which they had voiced with their tongues and by which they kept others from good: ﴿Then let them produce﴾, meaning, on whatever assumption they choose, ﴿a discourse﴾, that is, speech broken into parts and renewed over time, which they need not produce all at once, ﴿like it﴾, that is, like the Qur'an in eloquence, soundness of meaning, reports of the unseen both of what has happened and what will happen as they are, and wisdom.

Since the intent here is simply to make the deniers unable (*ta'jiz*), without the restriction of gathering together as in "Glory be to Him", because the revelation of this surah was among the first of what was revealed, He challenged them to produce the like of it in installments (*tanjim*) and in application to events, whether in surahs, verses, or less than that, renewing and recurring one thing after another. This is what the word "occurrence" (*huduth*) indicates. For this reason He removed from them the pretence of assembling and calling on whomever they could muster. And because they were lying in their certainty that he had fabricated it, or in attributing it to something else, He indicated this by saying, rebuking them and urging them to engage in the counter-attempt: ﴿If they are﴾, that is, if they are firmly established in the state of ﴿being truthful﴾, that is, in the claim that he invented it himself little by little, being deeply rooted in that as they assert, whether they claim that he is a poet, a soothsayer, a madman, or anything else. For custom makes it impossible that one man from a people, who is their equal, should produce something that all of them cannot match. A rational person does not affirm anything unless he knows it, and their knowledge of this entails their ability to produce the like of what he brings. He ﷺ was their equal in eloquence, in homeland, and in lineage, and some of them surpassed him in writing, in composing poetry, in associating with scholars, in practising sermons and epistles, and in other things. So he could not produce what they were unable to produce except by divine support, and this is what is meant by their denial. It is known from this, and from what has preceded of its kind dispersed through the surahs that contain its like, that the thing challenged in each surah is not the thing challenged in the other. And God is the Guide.

These preceding categories of their denial can be taken as assuming belief in God with His attributes of perfection. Then He followed them with an oath on the assumption of denial of the Creator (*ta'til*), for if there is no god there is no messenger, and so denial follows. Then He followed that with another oath, on the assumption of affirming God but with weakness through partnership (*shirkah*). Since partnership may come from the speaker or from others, He first mentioned what pertains to the speaker according to his own claim, and He mentioned the assumption of his partnership in creation, then in controlling the treasuries, then in writing, then in hearing secrets, then in the weakness of his capacity through contentment with the lowest kind.

When their disgrace through the challenge (*tahaddi*, the challenge to produce a comparable Qur'an) had already passed, and for them the disgrace of contradiction was less than the disgrace of counter-composition (*mu'arada*, producing an equal rival text), they used to put the former before the latter. So not one of them ever spoke, on any day, a word of the kind that could oppose it, knowing that they would thereby come to a shame whose stain could never be washed away, as happened to Musaylima. This is because they were the most intelligent of the Arabs. The sense, as the context indicates, was: "Indeed you are equal to them with respect to God's bringing you into existence. He, glorified is He, is the Creator of them just as He is the Creator of you, and you have no special status from Him according to their claim. Is He the Creator of them just as He is the Creator of you? Then it would be incumbent upon them to bring the like of what you bring." This was on the assumption that they acknowledged God and claimed that He (ﷺ) was lying. He, glorified is He, countered this, as a rebuke to them and a manifestation of disgraces more shameful than what they fled from, namely counter-composition, by His words, on the assumption that they were deniers of the Deity or claimed to be gods themselves: ﴿Or were they created﴾, that is, their creation occurred in this perfectly fashioned manner, ﴿from nothing?﴾, so that they would be opposed to clear reason, since the dependence of the created upon the Creator is a necessity of the name, just as its dependence upon the created thing is. This is so that it would be conceded to them that you bring what they cannot counter, because you are stronger than them by being dependent upon a Creator, while they are not dependent upon anything; or so that they would thereby be stronger and higher than you, and thus have arrogance over you. ﴿Or are they the creators?﴾, that is, the ones who possess this attribute, so that they would have created themselves in order to be partners by this, and then the Creator and the created would be one. This is like the division before it in not being dependent upon anything. Or the establishment of this attribute for them would necessitate that they be confident in what they say and arrogant toward you. If they claim that, then the lowest of creatures would judge them to be insane.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 52, verse 36:

﴿Or were they created of nothing?﴾ That is, as partners [in creation with Allah]? ﴿Or did they create the heavens and the earth?﴾ So they would then know about what is in them with comprehensive and certain knowledge, to the extent that they would know that you had fabricated it, so that they could refute it and mock it.

Since the implied sense is: none of that happened, so that they would have no doubt in what they say about you, he followed it with His saying: ﴿Rather, they have no certainty﴾. That is, they have no kind of certainty by which they could settle upon one thing, either because it is the truth, or so that they would know that this disgraceful consequence applies to them, and so they would refrain from such things.

﴿Am ʿindahum﴾ — that is, exclusively for them and not for anyone else — ﴿khazāʾinu﴾ ("treasuries"). Since the mention of mercy is not required by the central theme of the surah, which is punishment, it was not mentioned as it is in (Ṣād) and (Subḥān). So it was said: ﴿rabbika﴾ ("your Lord"), the One who showed you favour by sending you with this discourse, so that they would know that this which was affirmed through it is not from his own speech, because he has no authority over the treasuries except through them; thus their saying "you have fabricated it" would be valid, and then there would necessarily follow for them disgraceful consequences without end. Among them: that they would bring a discourse like it, nay better than it, from those treasuries. ﴿Am hum﴾ ("or is it they," not anyone else) ﴿al-muṣayṭirūn﴾ — that is, the overseers, the watchful guardians, the tyrants, the dominant rulers, the chiefs, the wise men, the scribes — so that they would be controllers of all things, as is the case with the secretaries of kings, so that they would know that you fabricated this reminder (p-29), because they did not write it to you.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 52, verse 38:

﴿Or do they have a ladder﴾ by which they ascend to the heaven, ﴿on which they listen﴾, that is, they deliberately strain to hear everything that happens in it and from it, ﴿therein﴾, that is, on that ladder and by means of it, just as some of those who attend the assemblies of kings in this world hear what takes place in them, so that they may be able to retain what comes from the king and thereby know that what they have said about you is true. And since one who is in this condition is able to bring wonders from there, He made the following statement a consequence of it: ﴿then let their listener bring a clear authority﴾, if they claim that, ﴿a clear authority﴾, that is, a compelling proof that is itself clear and manifest, making clear, because it comes from the heaven, the truth of what they accuse you of.

Since what has passed concerns the assumption of God's existence together with partners, and since their claim of offspring is very grave because it indicates His need and weakness, and their making Him to have daughters is graver because it indicates, along with weakness, folly, He showed the magnitude of this by turning to address them with their punishment, saying: ﴿Has He daughters while you have sons?﴾ That is, as you claim. ﴿And for you﴾ that is, specifically ﴿sons﴾, so that you would be stronger than Him and thus deny His messenger Muhammad (ﷺ) and reject his words without any proof, and so you would be secure from a punishment coming to you from Him, given His weakness and your strength. All these divisions are on the assumption of denial, whereas here the mention is of what is on the assumption of affirmation; the rejection occurred within them only because of an incidental matter that arose.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 52, verse 40:

Since the one who denies something may acknowledge that it comes from his god, and that his god is endowed with all the attributes of perfection, so that there is no partner for him, and that his denial is only due to a defect he cannot control, and a distress that has cast all its troubles upon him, [Allah] turned away from them, shifting to the first style, and said, addressing him (ﷺ) to honour his mention, to elevate his great rank, and to console him for what he knows of his noble self being free from it: ﴿Or do you ask them﴾, that is, O you of pure disposition, far from the places of accusation, ﴿for a reward﴾ for conveying what you have brought them, ﴿so that they are burdened by debt﴾, even if it is small, and al-maghram (debt, i.e. indebtedness) is the undertaking of what is not obligatory, ﴿heavily laden﴾, that is, a bearer has laid upon them a heavy burden because of that, so they deny the one who was the cause of this burden without any basis, in order to be relieved of the burden that he has brought upon them.

Since whoever claims exclusive possession of something envies whoever claims to share in it, He said: ﴿Or do they have the unseen﴾, that is, exclusively theirs, ﴿so that they write it down?﴾, that is, they renew for people the writing of all that is hidden from them of what benefits and harms them, so that they envy you for what you share with them of it, and thereby reject it, and attribute to you what they attribute to you, of which everyone knows your distance from it and your exemption from it.

Or do they intend, by this saying with which they accuse you, a scheme (*kaydan*), that is, a deception or a great harm, by which they seek to extinguish the light of God, in their own assumption, while knowing that you are truthful in it? Because of their intention to do that, the original structure would have been like this. But He said, generalizing and tying the ruling to the attribute: ﴿Then those who disbelieve﴾, that is, those who concealed the proofs, sometimes out of obstinacy and sometimes by turning away from contemplating them, ﴿they are﴾, that is, exclusively, ﴿the ones ensnared﴾, meaning that the burden of the scheme is confined to them, as it clings to them and cuts off their root, because whoever God is against is a loser. The nearest outcome for them from the manifest scheme was at Badr, about the end of years whose count equals the number of occurrences of *am* (أمْ) here, which is fifteen times, because Badr took place in the second year of the Hijrah (migration to Madinah), which was the fifteenth year of the Nubuwwah (prophethood). In it God arranged causes that compelled their striving toward their own destruction through matters that break customary patterns. So had they possessed insight, it would have sufficed them for guidance and for turning back from error and misguidance.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 52, verse 43:

When the sense was: "Is it thus the matter stands?", he balanced it with his saying: ﴿Or do they have a god﴾ who would prevent them from believing in Our Book, or on whom they rely for security from Our punishment, ﴿other than Allah﴾, who encompasses all the attributes of perfection, so that it is impossible in any way or on any supposition that there could be a god with Him. For this reason he joined to it His saying: ﴿Glory be to Allah﴾, that is, the Supreme King, who is exalted above having any trace of deficiency draw near to His court, ﴿above what they associate﴾ with Him, of idols and others. He (glorified is He) deferred this division, which is of the kind of partnership but with others, because it comes on the supposition of their affirming the Messenger (ﷺ), and because it is their religion which stopped them from guidance and caused them to fall into ruin, so that He would conclude it with the declaration of His own transcendence above the divisions, whereby the ultimate aim and objective is attained. The summary is that He (glorified is He) divided their condition in their rejection of the Qur'an into denial and other than denial. Since denial, which is attributing falsehood, that is, failing to correspond to reality, is either concerning the sending (of the messenger) or concerning the meanings, and what occurred in the sending (p-32) is either due to a deficiency in the Messenger or a deficiency in the Sender, and the deficiency in the Messenger is either due to something external to him or to something internal to him; since the external may be accompanied by a deficiency that enters into his essence, and since that may include something for which he is praised, even from one aspect, namely soothsaying (kihanah), He began with it; and He followed it with the internal matter corresponding to that, beginning with what may be praised, namely poetry. Since the claim that soothsaying, poetry and madness are combined in one person is, to the extreme degree, evidently self-contradictory, He followed these with the accusation of mockery against their intellects. Since the lie in the accusation of fabrication may be hidden, He followed it with its proof, namely the inability to produce a counterpart. Since He divided what they accused the Messenger of, He followed it with what they were obliged to accept regarding the sender. Since that is either by way of negation (ta'til) or not, and negation is more severe, He began with it, namely creation out of nothing. Since deficiency together with acknowledgment of existence is either by way of partnership or not, and the partnership is either one in which the denier is the partner or not, and the partnership of the denier is more firmly rooted in denial by its persistence; since the partnership of the denier is either in creation or not, and the first is either by creating the self or another, and partnership in creating the self is more closely connected, He began with it with His saying: ﴿Or were they created from nothing, or are they the creators?﴾ [al-Tur: 35]. Since partnership in other than creation is either in controlling the senses or not, and the second is either in controlling the Book, to which the reference is made by "the controller" (al-musaytir), or in controlling what they are commanded in it, to which the reference is made by "the ladder", or in the folly of the owner of the treasuries for his contentment with daughters; and since each division is more severe than what follows it, He arranged it thus. Since what returns (p-33) to denial has ended, He followed it with a refutation not for denial but for another matter; and since that matter is either from the one who brings or from the one to whom it is brought or from something else, what is from the one who brings is more closely connected, so He began with it, namely the burden (maghram). Since what is from the one to whom it is brought is either due to envy or otherwise, and the matter of envy is more severe, He began with it, namely partnership in offspring by what brings pride and leadership, which is knowledge of the unseen, looking in one respect to soothsaying with which He began in the division of denial; and the last of what is from something else, namely the partner who prevents them from acceptance. He mixed this division with the former even though it is a counterpart to what the denier supposed as a partner, because it is free of what accompanied those divisions of denial. This is the complete statement in refuting what was required of them concerning what they fabricated about the matter of the Qur'an. What you see of its rooting, division and detailed explanation has included an account of the powers of Allah and the wonders of His creation, which necessarily obliged them to monotheism, which in turn obliges affirmation of the message and submission to the truth, together with the inimitability in its arrangement, composition, refinement and facilitation and approximation, its great style being manifest in words that are the strung pearls, and meanings exalted above anything attached by nature or teaching, before which the most steadfast hearts nearly fly in bewilderment, and the most eloquent of the eloquent in the branches of its spirit become dazed and perplexed. So it was as Jubayr ibn Mut'im (may Allah be pleased with him) said, as narrated by al-Bukhari, Muslim, Abu Dawud, al-Nasa'i and Ibn Majah (may Allah be pleased with them all): "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited in the Maghrib prayer Surat al-Tur." Al-Bukhari said in (his book of) Tafsir: When he reached this verse, ﴿Or were they created from nothing, or are they the creators?﴾ [al-Tur: 35] ﴿Or did they create the heavens and the earth? Nay, they have no certainty﴾ [al-Tur: 36] ﴿Or do they have the treasuries of your Lord, or are they the controllers?﴾ [al-Tur: 37], "my heart nearly flew." Ibn Majah said: When I heard him recite ﴿Or were they created from nothing, or are they the creators?﴾ [al-Tur: 35] up to his saying ﴿then let their listener bring a clear authority﴾ [al-Tur: 38], "my heart nearly flew." And what al-Baghawi mentioned of this hadith was already mentioned at the beginning of the surah.

When the intended meaning was to comfort the heart of one who wished to answer their demands for the miraculous signs they proposed, out of hope for their faith, [the sense is]: We have recited to them in this surah and others among the verses, and We have displayed to them clear miracles, and We have brought out their contradictions in these divisions, with what shatters the lofty mountains, and We have made clear from their disgraceful conduct, through the excellence of its arrangement and the sweetness of its taste, the soundness of its meanings and the firmness of its structures, what shakes the firmly fixed, dissolves resolutions, relieves hardships, and turns away those of noble character from such shameful defects, because of the clear proofs they contain. But they, when We obligated them with the reversal [of their claims] that We imposed on them, do not believe. We have deceived them by blinding their insight, so they do not know that they are the ones being deceived. Then He joined to this His saying: ﴿And if they should see﴾, that is, witnessing directly, ﴿a piece﴾, a fragment, and it was said: pieces, its singular being *kisfah*, like *sidrah* and *sidr* (a lote-tree and lote-trees), ﴿of the sky﴾, by day, openly, ﴿falling down﴾, ﴿they would say﴾, out of obstinacy and stubborn persistence in rebellion, and their clinging to whatever doubts were available to them, as an imagining upon the intellects and a halting of those of judgment and understanding, the constant habit of the veteran in defending falsehood and obstinately opposing the truth, because of their long-established blindness of the hearts, with what We possess of the power to turn them away from the aspects of the matter: ﴿This is a cloud﴾. Then, if it were said to them that it differs from a cloud in its solidity, they would say: ﴿piled up﴾, that is, some of it has piled upon other parts until it became solid. For this reason He, on account of this condition, which indicates that they had reached such a degree of blindness of insight that even if every sign came to them they would not believe, connected to it His saying to His Prophet ﷺ and to those who follow him:

(p-35)

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 52, verse 45:

﴿So leave them﴾, that is, leave them in their worst state, ﴿until they meet﴾ the consequence of the evil of their deeds ﴿their Day﴾, just as He Himself comes toward them, because they deserve what is in it, ﴿which they are promised﴾, not in any other day, because what We have decided does not go forward or backward. ﴿They will be struck senseless﴾ (yuṣ‘aqūn) by death from the severity of the terrors and the magnitude of the quaking, just as the Children of Israel were struck senseless at the mount (al-Ṭūr). But We will keep them standing just as We kept those others standing, except at the blast of the Trumpet (al-Ṣūr), so that We may gather them to the reckoning which they deny. It is apparent that this day is the Day of Badr, for they were certain of victory on it, yet ﴿none of them could avail the other anything﴾, as Abū Sufyān ibn al-Ḥārith said: "It was nothing but that when we met them, we gave them our shoulders, and they killed us however they wished and took us captive however they wished."

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 52, verse 46:

﴿The day when their scheming will avail them nothing﴾ meaning, in no way whatsoever, ﴿against them﴾, that scheming with which they assail (the Qur'an) through these self-contradictory statements, ﴿at all﴾, meaning, providing any benefit in warding off something they dislike, whether death or anything else, as they imagine it will benefit them in other matters of this world by discouraging people from following the Qur'an through the slanders they attribute to it. ﴿Nor will they be helped﴾, meaning, no help from anyone will be renewed for them at any moment whatsoever.

[p-36] When this preceding statement made clear that the implied meaning is: indeed, for every wrongdoer on that Day there is a punishment that description cannot encompass, since being struck senseless (al-ṣa'q) is among the most severe forms of punishment, he followed it with a statement that emphasizes what they deny, namely: the believers will be given victory over them, while they are so numerous and powerful that no one can hope to overcome them, let alone those who are as weak and few as the believers are. ﴿And indeed﴾, where the expected wording would have been "for them," but he made it general and attached the judgment to a description, so he said: ﴿for those who did wrong﴾, meaning those who put things in other than their proper places, as they say about the Qur'an, practise through disobedience, and hold through polytheism and slander. ﴿a punishment short of that﴾, meaning other than the punishment of that difficult and bitter Day, or of a lower rank than it. If by "al-ṣa'q" is meant what happens after resurrection, then it refers to the punishment of al-barzakh (the intermediate state) in the graves. If it is meant to be death, then it refers to what they will suffer in this world at your hands, such as your withdrawal to the Anṣār in the abode of the Hijrah and the source of victory, and your becoming so strong that you will wage war against them and engage them in thrusting and striking. Thus, after having been at their mercy, you will become a thorn in their eyes, a bone in their throats, a slip for their feet, and a breaker of their plans. It also refers to the famine that befell them and to the expeditions in which you encountered them, such as the expedition of Ḥamzah, Lion of Allah and Lion of His Messenger, and of ʿUbaydah ibn al-Ḥārith and ʿUbayd Allah ibn Jaḥsh, which was a prelude to the Battle of Badr.

[p-37] Since some of them could see this, such as ʿUtbah ibn Rabīʿah, al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīrah and al-Naḍr ibn al-Ḥārith, and they would say: "By Allah, he is not a poet, nor a soothsayer, nor a sorcerer, nor a madman, and what he says will certainly have a consequence," he said: ﴿But most of them﴾, because of what they see of their large numbers, their good condition in this world and their strength, ﴿do not know﴾, meaning knowledge of your overpowering them will come to them afresh, because they have no knowledge at all until they witness that directly.

When the all-encompassing knowledge of the Sovereign, the Irresistible, is the greatest consolation to the friend (of God) and the greatest cause of dread to the enemy, He said, linking (this verse) to ﴿So leave them﴾ [al-Tur: 45], or to what its implied sense is: "Therefore be among those who know this, so that in it you will have the greatest consolation": ﴿And be patient﴾. That is, bring this reality into being (in your heart) so that you may endure what you are engaged in of conveying the Message and its burdens, including the harm of people and other things. Because he (the Prophet ﷺ) was in the station of turning away from the disbelievers, and turning away from them was harder for him than bearing the pain of warning them, even though it resulted in their denial and mockery, the concern here was intensified toward patience, so it was placed first. Also, turning away from them requires counting them as perishing, and that is the station of unification (jam'), and unification is not sound except with differentiation (farq). Therefore He placed the command to patience first, and mentioned the judgment (of God) to indicate that he is firmly established in the station of differentiation, just as he is deeply rooted in the station of unification. This differs from (the surah of) al-Muddaththir, whose context is warning, the consequence of which is the utmost harm. There the concern was intensified by placing the mention of the Deity first, with regard to annihilation from the perishing ones, even though he was directly calling them. He expressed (the matter) in a way that recalls good upbringing, for added consolation. This context required that He, glorified is He, encourage him by saying: ﴿For the judgment of your Lord﴾, that is, the One who does good to you, for He is the one who wills it, and had He not willed it, nothing of it would have occurred. So it is a favor from Him to you, a training for you, and an elevation along the ascending stages of wisdoms (p. 38). From this He drew the consequence, addressing what commonly prevails over the human disposition during some times of trial, of a kind of forgetfulness: ﴿Indeed you are under Our eyes﴾. He used the plural for what the "nun of majesty" (nun al-'azama, the royal "We") requires, and whose context this is; it is apparent in plurality, and it indicates that he is surrounded by angels whose sight is from His sight, glorified is He. Thus he is guarded and watched over by Him and by His hosts, and He acts in preserving him as one who has eyes encompassing what he guards from every direction.

When obedience was the greatest helper and the greatest comforter, and prayer was the greatest of it, He said: ﴿And glorify﴾, that is, perform the declaration of transcendence above any trace of every deficiency, with the heart, the tongue, and the limbs, while being clothed in ﴿the praise of your Lord﴾, that is, the One who does good to you. So affirm for Him every perfection along with declaring Him transcendent above every deficiency, so that nothing in His dominion occurs that He does not will, and He wills only what is perfect wisdom. ﴿When you arise﴾, that is, from the night, at all times that are the likely occasions of rising to worldly affairs and self-preoccupations, which are the hours of the day, given over to dispersal, (namely) the times of the Dawn, Noon and Afternoon prayers. The expression may also include glorifying (God) at every rising from a gathering, as an expiation for the gathering, which is: "Glory be to You, O Allah, and praise be to You; I bear witness that there is no god but You; I seek Your forgiveness and turn to You in repentance." Indeed, it expiates whatever occurred in the gathering, as narrated by Abu Dawud and al-Tirmidhi, who said: "Hasan sahih gharib," and by al-Nasa'i and Ibn Hibban in his Sahih, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet (ﷺ).

[p. 39]

﴿And during the night﴾, which is the place of stillness and rest, ﴿glorify Him﴾ likewise, in intention and in speech whenever you awaken, and in action through the Maghrib and 'Isha' prayers and the night prayer. Because of its greatness, he stated this explicitly and placed it before the verb. The pronoun refers back to the noun governed by the genitive (al-mudaf ilayhi, "the second term of the construct phrase"). He pointed to the tahajjud (the night vigil prayer) after its inclusion in what precedes it, with his words ﴿and at the setting of the stars﴾. That is, glorify Him at the time when they set, that is, when they have gone down. This is from the last part of the night, in its second half. The closer one comes to dawn, the more elevated the act is and the more likely it is to be answered.

The reading with fath, جمع دابر (dabir, "the last part" of something), points to nearness to dawn. That is, at its tails, when the stars fade or set. This is most fitting and most appropriate for the dawn prayer, whether sunnah or fard, because it is truly the time of their setting. Thus the worship of the morning becomes an act urged upon the believer twice, honoring it and magnifying its rank. For that protects from the descending punishment and grants victory over the enemy who advances in armor, the openly hostile and the deceitful hypocrite. The end of the surah has returned to its beginning, and its separated parts to its connected parts, through the descent of punishment upon the wrongdoer and its distance from the obedient, safe believer. And God is the Granter of success.
